The hook and the deny rules are policy a process can bypass (git commit --no-verify; a CC session with hooks off). value.assumption_check: FOUR, named with their standing. (1) That cgroup ancestry distinguishes the three callers. MEASURED for two of three on 2026-09-13: a rack-launched gate sits under a cairn-*.service unit (cairn/tools/cgroup already reads /proc/self/cgroup and the launchers proof test_ground_loop_survives_its_caller depends on it), and this CC session sits under the superclaude scope (the OOM cap in superclaude is a cgroup cap, memory claude-oom-kills-the-box). UNMEASURED: Akien's login shell on a pty reads as session-N.scope with no cairn unit above it; the door's proof measures all three, and the first tooth to write is that one. (2) That a CC launched OUTSIDE superclaude reads as Akien. TRUE by construction and it is a HOLE, not an assumption to resolve here: the launcher is the fix (superclaude is the one door to a CC session, memory rescue-service), carried in the ticket as owed physics. (3) That one journal file appended per write does not turn the record repos into a commit-per-write storm. The journal is ONE file per repo root (CairnCommons/.artifact-journal.jsonl and cairn/.artifact-journal.jsonl), appended, committed with the records it describes by the same commit the pre-commit hook inspects. (4) That 'record of truth' is an enumerable set. It is, today: tickets/, troubles/, decisions/, questions/, slates/, ideas/ under CairnCommons and every state.json, history.json, intention+why.json and validations/*.json under cairn/ (census 2026-09-13: 839 files). The set is DECLARED in cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json, and the rename ticket collapses it to one extension so the declaration becomes a glob.
value.builder_check: Questions a Haiku-level builder would need answered, and the answer each gets written into the ticket's how: (1) What exactly is the journal entry schema? {path (repo-relative), sha_before (sha256 of bytes or 'absent'), sha_after, verb (one of: cast, append, seal, clear, ruling, hand-edit, rename, bulk), caller {class: gate|cc|akien|unknown, cgroup: raw path, unit: cairn-*.service or null}, stack: [top 6 frames as file:line:function], why: free text from the caller, count: int (1 unless bulk), at: ISO-8601 UTC, prev: sha256 of the previous entry's canonical JSON or 'genesis', entry: sha256 of this entry's canonical JSON with entry=''}. (2) Where does the journal live and how is it found from a record path? Walk up from the record to the nearest of the two repo roots; the journal is <root>/.artifact-journal.jsonl. (3) What does the hook actually compare? For every staged file matching jurisdiction.json: sha256 of the STAGED blob == the last journal entry's sha_after for that path, else refuse with the path, both shas, and the one-line fix (`cairn artifact hand-edit <path> --why`). (4) How is the caller class decided? Read /proc/self/cgroup via cairn.tools.cgroup; a segment matching cairn-*.service → gate; a segment matching the superclaude scope name (read from launchers/superclaude, never hard-coded) → cc; a session-*.scope with a controlling tty and no cairn unit above → akien; anything else → unknown, and unknown is a journaled entry AND a raised trouble, never a silent write. (5) Which existing doors become callers, at which line? Listed in the ticket by path: validation store (cairn/devices/tester store), history append (cairn/tools/base history door), ticket cast (skills/sorted resolve), trouble clear (TroubleDevice.clear), ruling open (cairn/machines/ruling). Each replaces its write_text with artifact.write and passes its own verb. (6) What about the 145 other write sites? They are the rename ticket's job; this ticket lands the door and the five callers, and the hook reds the rest at their next commit — that red is the rename ticket's worklist, by design. (7) Is the Claude Code deny rule part of this ticket? Yes: .claude/settings.json gains permissions.deny for Edit/Write on the jurisdiction globs, and the existing deletegate PreToolUse hook on Bash learns the same globs for redirections and sed -i. Both are defense in depth over the pre-commit check, which is the one that counts.
value.collision_check: Judged over the whys. Law 6 says a tool has users, not owners, and gates nothing at its own address; the door is a tool and the journal is the HOLDER's state (berthed beside the records, in the repo that owns them), so the owner of each record class still gates through its verb and the door only records who came through. No collision. The harbor master's crossings journal records boats MOVING; this journal records bytes CHANGING — 481221f45884 (cursor hand-advanced to [PROVED] with no crossing behind it) is the case where they disagree, and disagreeing is the finding both exist to expose. A distinction, recorded. e2efd2771343's history_integrity sieve compares working copy against HEAD, which cannot tell a door write from a hand write until commit; this ticket gives it the missing baseline (the journal) and the sieve becomes a caller of the same check, not a rival. Law 5 ('the repo is itself the state of the machine') is what the journal serves: the journal is IN the repo. CP4 chafe check: Akien is himself a caller who gets refused at commit for a hand edit — that is the design he asked for ('then i'm on the hook for those edits'), and the escape route is the ruling verb, so 'paralysis or plaster' never arises.
value.falsifier_check: DONE when, measured by cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/: (1) write_text to a jurisdiction path from each of the three caller classes without the door is refused at commit by the pre-commit hook (the working-copy sha is not the journal's last sha_after) — three teeth, one per caller class, each a real subprocess under a fixture cgroup or the real one; (2) the door, called from a systemd --user transient unit, from this superclaude scope, and from a pty login shell, journals caller=gate|cc|akien respectively — measured, not read from a field; (3) a chain break (an entry edited or removed) is detected by replaying the chain from the first entry; (4) `cairn artifact hand-edit <path> --why` parks the diff, opens a ruling packet through `cairn ruling open`, and leaves the record byte-identical until the ruling is confirmed; the door reverts it on `cairn ruling` refusal; (5) a proof's scratch record under a set_diagnostic_roots world never reaches the journal. WRONG INTENT if the door reads caller=unknown for any of the three in (2) — then identity must come from elsewhere and the journal is a log, not a gate. HORIZON: the three-caller measurement is the first proof written, before any hook; if it fails the ticket routes back to Akien with the measurement, not a workaround.
value.missing_check: TWO points were asserted wrapped and are not, and both are recorded as the ticket's IOUs rather than cast as done. (a) The physics floor: the pre-commit hook and the Claude Code deny rules are POLICY the same process can bypass (git commit --no-verify; a CC session with hooks disabled). The real physics is the record roots owned by a second unix user with the door as the only sudo-relay path — filed as owed_physics on the ticket with the sudo relay named as the mechanism (memory sudo-relay-self-serve-ops), not built in this ticket. (b) Callers that are in-process machines: the validation store, history append, ticket cast and trouble clear are today functions, not processes; they resolve to whichever unit hosts them. That is the RIGHT answer (the gate is the owner, Law 6) but it means 'which door verb' comes from the call stack the journal records as provenance, and the stack is a claim the caller makes. The WHO is kernel truth; the WHY is testimony. The ticket says so in its how, and the counting block (third ticket) is what makes an unusual WHY visible over time.

value.better_approach: Looked. Deny-rules alone (permissions.deny on Edit/Write) are one line and zero build — but blind to Bash, which is the path this session was told to prefer; a hook on Bash alone is blind to git checkout/stash/merge. The pre-commit check is the smallest single point that sees all three, so the door + journal + hook is the minimal shape that is physics rather than policy. The physics upgrade beyond it — the record roots owned by a second unix user, doors through the sudo relay — is filed as the IOU, not built now.
value.hidden_assumption: That cgroup ancestry is readable from inside every caller and distinguishes the three: a CC session must actually sit under a superclaude scope (measured for the ground loop; not yet measured for a CC launched outside superclaude, e.g. from a bare terminal — that reads as Akien, which is the hole to close with the launcher), and an in-process machine caller under systemd must resolve to its unit. Also that the journal can live in git beside the records without every door write producing a commit-per-write storm — it appends to one file.
value.prior_art: In-house: 55dc1f3d799b (validation store door is the only path, PROVED — one class), e2efd2771343 (state/history append door + history_integrity sieve comparing working copy against HEAD — two classes, wrong baseline: a door write and a hand write look identical until commit), 23089d52d805 (casting rides a door, TICKETME:waiting), 47b9767d6faa (relational state through db_domain). This intent generalizes them into one door with caller identity; the per-class doors keep their verbs and become callers. Field: git's own object model (content-addressed, hash-chained) is the pattern the journal cites; Friston's free-energy loop is the pattern the third ticket cites — the door is a prediction ('a record changes only through a door') with a residual that escalates.
value.real_collision: Law 6 vs 'a tool has users, not owners': the door is a TOOL (no state of its own — the journal is the holder's, berthed beside the records it guards), so it gates nothing at its own address; the OWNER of each record class still gates through its verb. No collision with the harbor master's crossings journal: that records boats moving, this records bytes changing, and 481221f45884 is exactly the case where the two disagree and should. Not exclusive-and-terminal anywhere — a distinction to record: the harbor journal says what MOVED, the artifact journal says what was WRITTEN and by whom.

deviations_from_the_cast_falsifier: (1) cast as three teeth, one per caller class; built as ONE class-independent tooth (test_a_record_edited_around_the_door_is_refused_at_the_commit_question) — the commit question reads bytes against the journal and never asks who edited, so a per-class tooth would measure nothing the one tooth does not. Clause (2) is where the class is measured.

(2) cast as 'a pty login shell' for akien; built as the LIVE processes in session-N.scope / app-*.scope (four measured at seal: pids 1808, 1809, 2525119, 2525662 → akien), because a pty shell spawned by this session is a child of the superclaude scope and correctly reads cc by ancestry — a forged akien would have been the hollow tooth. gate is measured under a real transient cairn-proof-artifact-<pid>.service; cc is this session's scope and a plain child of it.

(4) cast as 'opens a ruling packet through cairn ruling open'; built as PARK: hand-edit restores the journaled bytes and parks the proposed bytes under the door (`cairn artifact parked`); approve(id, words) is accepted only from a process measured akien (refused from cc by measurement in the proof), refuse discards. Why: `cairn ruling open` needs his verbatim words, which a park does not yet have — the park is what waits for them; the ruling packet is opened by him or on his words at approve time, not authored by the door.
the caller CLASS is kernel truth (cgroup ancestry); the call stack Akien asked for rides the entry as testimony (top six frames) and never decides trust.

measured.ancestry: systemd-run --user --scope moves a child into a new scope but does not reparent it — a scope CC forges to look like a desktop app still has the claude process (superclaude-<pid>.scope) as an ancestor and reads cc. Measured 2026-09-13 in the proof (tooth 'a scope CC forges to look like a desktop app STILL reads as cc — by ancestry').
measured.escape_not_closed: a scope plus a double fork (parent exits, child reparented to pid 1) would break the ancestry walk — that child reads by its own scope, and if the scope is named like an app it reads akien. Not built against; recorded here as the door's known escape, beside the two the cast already named (git commit --no-verify; CC launched outside superclaude).
measured.gate_matches_command_text: bin/cmd/artifactgate reads the Bash command TEXT for a redirect/mv/cp/rm/sed -i/python open-for-write aimed at a record; a heredoc that merely mentions such a pattern is refused too (n=1 this session, a proof edit) — the trade is a split command, never a lost write.
